'''Maria-Carme T. Calderer''' ([[Berga]], 1951)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carme Calderer |url=https://wimmn.math.umn.edu/womens-history-month-2020/carme-calderer |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=wimmn.math.umn.edu |language=en-US}}</ref> is a professor of mathematics at [[University of Minnesota]]. Her research concerns [[applied mathematics]].

==Career==
Calderer received her Ph.D. from [[Heriot-Watt University]] in 1980.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=40811|title=Maria-Carme Calderer}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]] from 1984 to 1987, first as a postdoctoral researcher, and then as a visiting professor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.umn.edu/newsletter/2002/|title=University of Minnesota - Newsletter of the School of Mathematics January 2002|accessdate=Feb 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150123205005/http://www.math.umn.edu/newsletter/2002/|archive-date=January 23, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> She worked at [[Penn State]] from 1989 until 2001, when she joined the faculty of [[University of Minnesota]].

==Awards and honors==
In 2000 Calderer received the Teresa Cohen Service Award from [[Penn State University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.psu.edu/about/giving/cohen-service|title=Teresa Cohen Service Award|location=[[Penn State University]]|accessdate=Feb 1, 2015}}</ref>

In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=2015-02-02 |archive-date=2018-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2022 she will become a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], "For being a role model nationally and internationally due to her outstanding research contributions in the mathematics of materials; for her long record of mentoring, advising, and supervising women in applied mathematics; and for her leadership role in the mathematics community by organizing conferences, workshops, and thematic years."<ref>{{Cite web|title=2022 Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards-awm-fellows-2022-awm-fellows/}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Calderer was raised in [[Berga, Spain]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Jensen |first=Jill |date=March 6, 2012 |title=Data shows men dominate science and engineering faculty at the U |url=http://www.mndaily.com/2012/03/06/data-shows-men-dominate-science-and-engineering-faculty-u |newspaper=Minnesota Daily |location=[[University of Minnesota]] |access-date=Feb 1, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120518234651/http://www.mndaily.com/2012/03/06/data-shows-men-dominate-science-and-engineering-faculty-u |archive-date=May 18, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She is married to [[Douglas Arnold]], one of her fellow professors of mathematics at [[University of Minnesota]].

==Selected publications==
*[[Patricia E. Bauman|Bauman, Patricia]]; Calderer, M. Carme; Liu, Chun; Phillips, Daniel The phase transition between chiral nematic and smectic A∗ liquid crystals. ''Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal.'' 165 (2002), no. 2, 161–186.
*Calderer, M. Carme; Liu, Chun Liquid crystal flow: dynamic and static configurations. ''SIAM J. Appl. Math.'' 60 (2000), no. 6, 1925–1949.
